objection.quote: The virtual cut partitions the large bin into two sub-sticks of length \(\tau\) each; the actual pieces of \(Q\) are a common refinement of those two sub-sticks.
objection.witness: Counterexample: take n=2, so the large bin has length 4 and τ=2. Put both allowed cuts in it, at positions 1.5 and 2.5. Then Q consists of lengths 1.5, 1, 1.5, all at most τ, but the virtual midpoint 2 lies inside the actual piece [1.5,2.5]. Thus Q is not a refinement of the two halves.
objection.load_bearing: The subcase relies on splitting Q into refinements of the two halves and applying induction to them. The false refinement claim removes the basis for that induction, leaving arbitrary interleavings untreated.
